title: canary-human-factor-observatory-and-ops-experiments-wip
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working notebook for an experiment-style approach to canaries that centers human factors and operator observability. The goal is to run small-ish canaries that produce interpretable human signals (friction, confusion, trust) in addition to telemetry, and to iterate on ops patterns that reduce manual toil during progressive exposure.

Context / Why this dir:
- Lots of rollout docs are focused on traffic splits, telemetry, and automation. We need a counterpart that treats on-call humans (stewards, product owners, CS reps) as first-class signals: what they observe matters and is actionable.
- Working hypothesis: proactively surfacing human-class signals (support tickets, steward sentiment, edit distance of fallback prompts, frequency of manual interventions) improves rollback precision and reduces blast radius.

Audience:
- Oncall/stewards, product owners, release engineers, solutions engineers, SREs who staff canaries and A/Bs. Also useful for SEs planning human-in-the-loop experiments.

Quick TL;DR (operational):
- Run micro-canaries with 0.5–5% traffic using a dedicated steward pair.
- Instrument four human-centric signals and put simple thresholds in the steward dashboard.
- Run a 72-hour human-observability window (H-obs window) where stewards report twice per day via short form.
- If human signals exceed thresholds OR telemetry triggers, follow the rollback lattice (appendix).

Human signals we track (prototype set):
- Steward intervention rate: fraction of responses where steward performed manual edit, re-prompt, or escalation. (target < 1.5% for stable canary)
- Support frictions per 10k users: number of tickets flagged as "model-behavior" (keyword/manual label).
- Confidence erosion indicator: number of users who enabled fallback/manual mode after seeing degraded outputs.
- Narrative drift complaints: count of qualitative short notes flagged by CS as "tone/incorrect/unsafe".

How to capture these cheaply:
- Steward quick-forms: a 6-question Google Form for every steward shift (link in linked_artifacts). Questions are short multiple choice + optional 1-line observation.
- Slack micro-tags: instruct stewards to use message prefix "[HOBS]" for any thread about canary anomalies (makes automated search easier).
- Support queue classifier: lightweight keyword filter and triage tag (manual review for first 48 hours).
- Product follow-up shorthand: if steward re-runs a prompt, paste original and edited outputs in a shared doc called "HOBS-edits-YYYYMMDD".

Sample steward shift protocol (30–45m shift):
- 0–10m: review the steward dashboard (latency, error, top failing slices, human-form summaries)
- 10–30m: spot check 10 random user sessions or recent support threads, mark any with tags (misinfo, safety, hallucination, latency, incoherence)
- 30–40m: fill quick-form, ping primary on-call if any items are critical
- 40–45m: handoff notes + post to #canary-ops with short 3-line summary.

Experiment matrix (ops-oriented, sketch):
- Variant A (control): standard telemetry-only canary.
- Variant B (human-observatory): same traffic but with steward pair and H-obs forms + slack tags.
- Variant C (auto-hybrid): human observability + automatic lightweight mitigation (re-route to smaller model on steward flag)
Notes on design: rotate which product area runs Variant B vs A to avoid bias in steward sensitivity.

Decision heuristics (starter):
- Safety-critical alarm: ANY steward label "unsafe" OR user-visible harm -> immediate rollback to previous stable model and incident call.
- Elevated human friction (2x baseline steward intervention rate for 12h OR >5 tickets per 10k users in 24h) -> pause traffic ramp and escalate to product + SRE for triage.
- Low-level drift (small but consistent rise in narrative drift complaints) -> run evaluation suite, hold ramp; consider prompt-tuning rollback.

Comms templates (short forms):
- 1-line triage ping (Slack):
  [HOBS][URGENT] Model X Canary @ 3% — steward intervention rate 2.7% over last 4h (baseline 0.6%). Escalating to product-oncall.
- User-facing temporary note (support macro):
  Thanks for flagging — we99re investigating and have temporarily routed some requests to a fallback to reduce recurrence.

Simulation scenarios to run before the live canary (ops tabletop style):
- Scenario: gradual tone drift detected by CS after 18h; steward reports 1.8% edits in last 6h. Walkthrough: who calls incident? When do we pause?
- Scenario: sudden spike in latency that correlates with a downstream dependency; steward reports more manual retries. Walkthrough: can we reroute to a cheaper model variant? Rollback vs. traffic shaping?
- Scenario: A/B confusion — two cohorts see different phrasing and some customers report inconsistent UX. Walkthrough: statistical checks + manual review cadence.

Data instrumentation checklist (minimum viable):
- Steward intervention metric (event logged with steward id, timestamp, original text, edited text, reason tag)
- Support ticket ingestion + basic NLP triage labels (safety/hallucination/UX)
- Quick-form aggregation endpoint (CSV + dashboard card)
- Slack tag archival (searchable for last 90 days)
- Link each human signal to the experiment record in the rollout console (experiment id/Jira key).

Open questions / risks (brain dump):
- Privacy: steward paste of user conversations into shared docs — need a sanitized pattern or ephemeral storage. Who owns redaction?
- Steward bias: different stewards have different tolerance; we need calibration sessions (golden examples) and inter-rater reliability checks.
- Operational overhead: are we adding too much friction for low-signal features? How to measure net benefit?
- Alert noise: human signals can spike during benign load — need smoothing and rolling windows to avoid flip-flopping.

Calibration plan (1-month pilot):
- Week 0: baseline telemetry-only canary runs on 3 small features to collect metrics. Recruit 6 stewards and run calibration training (30m).
- Week 1–2: run Variant B on 2 features (randomized) with steward pair shifts; collect quick-form responses and compare to telemetry.
- Week 3: run tabletop for top-2 observed failure modes; adjust decision thresholds.
- Week 4: run a blind evaluation (stewards see masked traffic) to test bias; write brief retrospective.

Appendix A — rollback lattice (short):
- Level 0: soft pause of ramp and increased steward ops cadence.
- Level 1: pause + partial rollback for specific slices (region/customer segment).
- Level 2: full rollback to last stable model + incident call.
- Level 3: safety lockdown (disable feature and notify legal/CS in parallel).

Appendix B — steward calibration checklist (short):
- 6 example prompts with labeled correct/acceptable/unsafe outputs (golden set)
- Short calibration scoring rubric (0=no action, 1=note, 2=edit, 3=escalate)

Immediate next steps (for this doc):
- Finalize quick-form link + attach to linked_artifacts (Lena)
- Create steward onboarding 30m slide deck (Miguel)
- Add instrumentation tickets: JIRA-3241 (support ingestion), JIRA-3242 (steward-event logging) (Samir)
- Schedule 2x tabletop sessions in Dec for Product + SRE + CS (Priya)

Notes to self: keep this intentionally lightweight — main value is making human observations quickly actionable. Will iterate into a more formal playbook if pilot signals are promising.

-- end of working doc --
